plain: The analysis combined 5 studies measuring 2 correlated outcomes. In the order shown on the page, the pooled effects were 0.353 and −0.339. Their 95% confidence intervals were 0.238 to 0.469 and −0.512 to −0.167. These intervals describe uncertainty in average effects, not the range of effects in a new study. Clinical importance and causality cannot be determined from this summary.
methods: Complete paired outcome vectors were analysed using a multivariate normal random-effects model with known within-study covariance matrices. The unstructured between-study covariance was estimated by restricted maximum likelihood; outcome means were estimated by generalised least squares. The app uses Cholesky-parameterised Nelder–Mead optimisation, boundary refinements, and an exact restricted-likelihood solution for two studies. Mean standard errors come from the inverse sum of inverse total covariance matrices. Marginal 95% confidence limits use the normal Wald formula, mean plus or minus the normal quantile times its standard error, without a Hartung–Knapp adjustment. The joint plot uses a bivariate normal confidence ellipse. Effects are used on their supplied scale without transformation or continuity correction. Incomplete rows are omitted by the app; positive-definite within-study covariance matrices and at least two complete studies are required. Between-study correlation is undefined if either between-study variance is zero. The restricted log likelihood includes the outcome-design normalisation. No hypothesis-test p-values, heterogeneity Q or I-squared statistics, or prediction intervals are computed. Analyses were run in allmeta multivariate-ma <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: There were 5 studies and 2 outcomes. In page order, the pooled estimates were 0.353 (95% CI 0.238 to 0.469) and −0.339 (95% CI −0.512 to −0.167). Between-study standard deviations were 0.1083 and 0.1807. Between-study correlation was 0.609. The restricted log likelihood was 3.692.
flags: Tests for small-study effects would be underpowered; none were performed.
